user.title: Configure Energiemanager GSI
user.description: Map the grid connection and optional PV/battery sensors. Positive grid power means import; negative means export. Net export preserves other household demand and battery charging; PV budget distributes generation. PMAX limits both strategies.

data.surplus_min_battery_soc: Battery reserve SOC for surplus mode
data.configure_points_first: Create Modbus/MQTT points first (assign grid meter later)

data_description.grid_power_entity: Required. Net power measured at the grid connection point.
data_description.grid_limit_kw: Hard maximum permitted grid import in kW.
data_description.grid_sensor_timeout_s: Maximum permitted age of the critical grid measurement. Older data activates fail-safe.
data_description.invert_grid_power: Enable if the source reports import as negative and export as positive.
data_description.invert_pv_power: Enable if PV generation is reported as a negative value.
data_description.battery_power_entity: Optional battery power sensor. Internally positive means discharge and negative means charge.
data_description.invert_battery_power: Enable if the source uses the opposite battery sign convention.
data_description.battery_soc_scale: Use percent for 0..100 % sources, or fraction for unitless 0..1 sources.
data_description.surplus_min_battery_soc: At the reserve threshold, net export blocks consumers. The existing PV budget strategy switches to Normal.
data_description.grid_power_factor: Raw state × factor, then conversion of the sensor unit. Example: 5000 W × 0.1 = 500 W. Factor 1 leaves the value unchanged.
data_description.pv_power_factor: Raw state × factor, then conversion of the sensor unit. Example: 5000 W × 0.1 = 500 W. Factor 1 leaves the value unchanged.
data_description.battery_power_factor: Raw state × factor, then conversion of the sensor unit. Example: 5000 W × 0.1 = 500 W. Factor 1 leaves the value unchanged.
data_description.battery_soc_factor: Raw state × factor, followed by the selected percent/fraction conversion. Result must be 0–100%.
data_description.surplus_strategy: Net export: controlled actual demand − grid import − battery discharge. PV budget retains the existing generation-based budget. Battery discharge can only be excluded when a battery power sensor is configured.
data_description.house_power_entity: Only for a meter of total household demand. Leave empty for an import/export grid meter: house = grid + PV + battery discharge (charging negative). Base demand = house − all consumers.
data_description.house_power_factor: Raw state × factor before unit conversion.
data_description.configure_points_first: Allows setup without a grid sensor. Control stays in fail-safe until a valid meter is assigned.

user.title: Add controllable load
user.description: Add a load to the central controller. Leave output entities empty for dry-run-only operation. EVSE fields are only used for the EVSE load type.

data_description.load_name: Unique name used by the controller.
data_description.load_type: Modulating = numeric power output, switch = all-or-nothing load, EVSE = kW target converted to amps.
data_description.priority: 1 is the highest priority. Equal priorities share available power.
data_description.min_kw: Technical minimum power. For switch loads this is automatically set to rated power.
data_description.max_kw: Maximum controllable or rated load power.
data_description.default_request_kw: Used when no request entity is configured. Enter 0 to request max_kw.
data_description.actual_power_entity: Optional measured load power. If unavailable, the controller conservatively estimates from the previous target.
data_description.actual_sensor_timeout_s: Maximum permitted age of the actual-power measurement. Older data is discarded and the core falls back to its target estimate.
data_description.invert_actual_power: Invert the sign of the actual-power sensor.
data_description.request_entity: Optional. A power sensor requests that kW amount; an on/off entity requests max_kw when on.
data_description.availability_entity: Optional on/off entity. Unknown or unavailable blocks this load.
data_description.output_entity: Power setpoint: number/input_number. Switching load or separate enable: switch, input_boolean, number, input_number, select or input_select.
data_description.enable_entity: Power setpoint: number/input_number. Switching load or separate enable: switch, input_boolean, number, input_number, select or input_select.
data_description.output_unit: Choose A or W (also kW/MW). Auto uses the entity unit, or A for EVSE. Amps use the phases and voltage below; P = phases × voltage × I at power factor 1.
data_description.safe_output_value: Numeric value written at zero target for a modulating load. Usually 0. If it is outside the number range, configure a separate enable entity.
data_description.peak_shaving_enabled: Allow this load to be reduced for PMAX.
data_description.surplus_enabled: Allow this load to receive PV surplus in surplus mode.
data_description.start_margin_kw: Additional budget required before an off load may start.
data_description.stop_margin_kw: Additional budget required to keep an already running load after minimum on time.
data_description.min_on_time_s: Comfort/runtime constraint. PMAX can still override it.
data_description.settling_time_s: After a target change, increases are blocked until this time expires; reductions remain allowed.
data_description.evse_phases: Number of phases used for kW-to-A conversion.
data_description.evse_voltage_v: Phase-to-neutral voltage used for kW-to-A conversion.
data_description.evse_pause_current_a: Current value that represents pause/off. It must be below the technical minimum.
data_description.actual_power_factor: Raw state × factor, then conversion of the sensor unit. Example: 5000 W × 0.1 = 500 W. Factor 1 leaves the value unchanged.
data_description.request_factor: Raw state × factor, then conversion of the sensor unit. Example: 5000 W × 0.1 = 500 W. Factor 1 leaves the value unchanged. Boolean demand states are not scaled.
data_description.command_on: Value for a numeric switching load or separate enable, e.g. 12. For select/input_select use the exact option text. switch/input_boolean uses turn_on/turn_off.
data_description.command_off: Value for a numeric switching load or separate enable, e.g. 14. For select/input_select use the exact option text. switch/input_boolean uses turn_on/turn_off.

user.title: Measurement/control point
user.description: Creates a freely assignable HA entity. MQTT uses the broker configured in Home Assistant. sensor reads measurements, number writes setpoints, switch sends configurable ON/OFF values.

data.name: Name
data.protocol: Connection: modbus = Modbus TCP, mqtt = HA broker
data.kind: Entity: sensor = measurement, number = setpoint, switch = ON/OFF

data.name: Name
data.protocol: Connection: modbus = Modbus TCP, mqtt = HA broker
data.kind: Entity: sensor = measurement, number = setpoint, switch = ON/OFF

mqtt.title: MQTT
mqtt.description: Concrete topics without +/#. Optional JSON path, e.g. data.power or values.0. Without a readback topic, state is assumed. Old retained measurements are ignored. {detail}

modbus.title: Modbus TCP
modbus.description: Zero-based addresses. holding/input: FC3/FC4, coil/discrete: FC1/FC2. big = normal, little = swapped. HA value = raw × factor; writes use the inverse. State timeout must cover polling + response timeout. Setup never writes. {detail}
